newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank eases late, baht steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank eases late, baht steady.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased on Thursday afternoon amid inflows of foreign capital to take advantage of the rising equity market, traders said.
The Thai overnight interbank offered rate was quoted at 8.50-9.00 percent late on Thursday, easing from 9.25-9.75 percent earlier in the day.
Dealers said liquidity was expected to tighten for the rest of the week as the Bank of Thailand has scheduled a $120 million bond auction for Friday aimed at mopping up liquidity.

Assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee said on Thursday that the authorities have monitored the money market and absorbed excessive liquidity in order to stabilise the overnight rate in a 9-11 percent range.

"The liquidity eased today with the banks and the big finance houses carrying cash but tomorrow I expect it to tighten to 9-10 percent tomorrow and next week to 9-11 percent," said a trader at Siam City Bank.
The baht eased during late afternoon transactions to 25.632/25.637 from 25.625/25.630 in the morning, traders said.
The bid/offer range on the one month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 7.00/7.50 satang per dollar from 6.50/7.50 in the morning but against 7.25/7.75 late on Wednesday.
"I think the swap is generally in line with the downward trend of interest rates, it may fall a bit further but not much," said a dealer at Thai Danu Bank.
